transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A trip around 15 minutes into a dishwasher cycle most often points to an electrical earth-leakage fault as the machine reaches its heating stage. The usual suspect is the heater/flow-through heating assembly; an intermittent fault there can explain why it does not trip on every run. The circulation pump or its wiring is the next possibility. A mains filter or incoming cable fault is less likely because those more often trip immediately. Do not use the dishwasher again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. Repeatedly resetting the electrics and trying another cycle is not safe. With the dishwasher switched off, isolated/unplugged and cool, you can only make these external checks:
1. Inspect the plug and visible mains lead for heat damage, cracking, crushing or dampness. Any sign of this means leave it isolated and tell the engineer.
2. Look for water on the floor or around the hose connections. Water reaching electrical parts can also cause an intermittent trip; do not remove panels or investigate internal wiring. The timing is useful evidence for the engineer: a trip when heating starts strongly favours the heater; during the initial wash/circulation phase favours the circulation pump; immediately on switching on favours the mains filter or supply wiring.

candidates: Heater or flow-through heater assembly leaking to earth once heating begins (high)
Circulation pump or its wiring developing an intermittent earth fault (medium)
Mains filter, supply cable or internal wiring fault (low)

reading.symptom: keeps tripping the electrics, usually about 15 minutes into a cycle

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Zanussi; model ZDT21006FA.
The fault they reported is: "keeps tripping the electrics, usually about 15 minutes into a cycle". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
